instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice in a strainer. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes and leave the lid on until you serve.
Tear the mushrooms into chunky, bite-size pieces, and trim off any tough stem ends. Roughly chop the garlic and pick the basil leaves off the stems.
Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until it smells good and is just starting to turn gold. Don't let it brown.
Add the vegetarian oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar. Stir for about 30 seconds, until the sugar has dissolved and the sauce is bubbling.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the mushrooms. Toss to coat them and cook for 3 minutes.
If the pan looks dry, add 2 tbsp of water at a time, up to about 1/4 cup in all. Keep cooking for 2 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and there's a little sauce in the pan.
Take the pan off the heat, add the basil, and toss until it wilts.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Slice the chilies thinly and put them in a small bowl. Serve with the rice, with the chilies on the table.
method_notes: The lead is Thai Cookbook's Pad Hed Nang Rom (4.5 from 6,358 reader reviews, as shown on the page), a quick garlic, oyster sauce and soy sauce stir-fry of oyster mushrooms finished with sweet basil. Hungry in Thailand's 20-minute Pad Hed uses the same sauce with a little white pepper and green onions. Oyster sauce is swapped for a vegetarian (mushroom) oyster sauce to keep it vegetarian and vegan, and the 6 to 8 chilies in the lead go on the side. Amounts are about doubled for four with rice.
